answer_text:
Let \(F_2=\langle a,b\rangle\) be the free group on two generators.

**Upper bound.**  
\(F_2\) is countable, since its elements are reduced finite words in
\(\{a^{\pm1},b^{\pm1}\}\). Hence the set of subgroups of \(F_2\) is a subset of
\(\mathcal P(F_2)\), so

\[
|\operatorname{Sub}(F_2)|\le 2^{\aleph_0}.
\]

**Lower bound.**  
Define a homomorphism

\[
\pi:F_2\to \mathbb Z,\qquad \pi(a)=1,\quad \pi(b)=0.
\]

Let \(K=\ker \pi\). By the Reidemeister–Schreier method, \(K\) is free with basis

\[
\{c_n=a^nba^{-n}:n\in\mathbb Z\}.
\]

For every subset \(S\subseteq \mathbb Z\), let

\[
H_S=\langle c_n:n\in S\rangle \le K\le F_2.
\]

These subgroups are all distinct. Indeed, if \(S\ne T\), say \(m\in S\setminus T\).
Since \(\{c_n\}_{n\in\mathbb Z}\) is a free basis of \(K\), there is a homomorphism
\(\varepsilon_m:K\to\mathbb Z\) with

\[
\varepsilon_m(c_m)=1,\qquad \varepsilon_m(c_n)=0\quad(n\ne m).
\]

Then \(\varepsilon_m(H_T)=0\), but \(\varepsilon_m(c_m)=1\), so \(c_m\notin H_T\).
Thus \(H_S\ne H_T\).

Therefore the map \(S\mapsto H_S\) injects \(\mathcal P(\mathbb Z)\) into the set of subgroups of \(F_2\), giving

\[
|\operatorname{Sub}(F_2)|\ge 2^{\aleph_0}.
\]

Combining the upper and lower bounds,

\[
|\operatorname{Sub}(F_2)|=2^{\aleph_0}.
\]

\[
\boxed{2^{\aleph_0}}
\]
